shortName: Western Michigan University Homer Stryker M.D. School of Medicine
additionalCoursework: There are no required prerequisite courses for admission to WMed. In addition to the above, we also recommend taking Medical Terminology to help your transition to medical school.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Our holistic, mission-aligned student selection process values a multitude of academic, medical, and life experiences and recognizes a wide range of both cognitive and non-cognitive attributes of applicants. Our classes include students from across the United States with a broad variety of backgrounds and experiences, all sharing a common purpose to achieve excellence in a stimulating, supportive, and collegial environment.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students may request a leave of absence for a period of up to one year. Students must complete all requirements for the MD degree within six years of matriculation. The associate dean for Educational Affairs may extend the degree completion time limit to more than six distinct academic years for students who are enrolled in other academic courses, pursuing additional scholarly activities, or enrolled in a dual-degree program.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Students participate in a variety of student organizations for professional development, personal growth, service, and fun. Student organizations include the Association of American Medical Colleges Organization of Student Representatives, American Medical Association Medical Student Section, American Medical Student Association, Student National Medical Association (SNMA), American Medical Women's Association, and the Latino Medical Student Association (LMSA). Student Council provides representation for every class. Leadership and advocacy opportunities on institutional committees include the Curriculum Committee, Global Health Committee, and numerous others. 

Nearly 100 student interest groups provide forums  in particular areas of medicine or extracurricular interests: https://wmed.edu/studentinvolvement

Student interest groups also provide informal mentorships in addition to the formal mentor programs: https://wmed.edu/learningcommunities

https://wmed.edu/studentlife
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
WMed is housed in a 350,000 square foot building located on the W.E. Upjohn M.D. Campus in downtown Kalamazoo. This is the primary site for medical education for the Foundations of Medicine courses. The downtown campus is within walking distance of housing, restaurants, theaters, and public transportation. The eight-story building underwent a $68 million renovation and expansion that opened in June 2014, and an additional $10 million renovation of research laboratories that opened in 2016. The educational facilities include two team-based learning halls, state-of-the-art Simulation Center, an auditorium, anatomy lab, research laboratories, four student Learning Communities and student commons, library, classrooms and conference rooms, ample open study space, fitness center, and administrative space.

Learn more about:
virtual tour: https://www.covecreekproductions.com/tours/wmed/
campus: https://wmed.edu/campus-safety-info
community: https://wmed.edu/livinginkalamazoo
medSchoolStudLife.housing: There is ample housing available near WMed in downtown Kalamazoo, an area that caters to young professionals. The majority of students choose to live within walking distance of campus in rental apartments, lofts, or homes. The Kalamazoo-Portage area has a low cost of living and offers a wide variety of attractive, affordable housing options for medical students, including students with families. WMed students enjoy that Kalamazoo's cost of living is below the national average. Learn more about living in Kalamazoo at: wmed.edu/livinginkalamazoo
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: WMed supports students from all backgrounds. All students have access to the many support systems available. There are also multiple clubs and organizations that provide support, advocacy, and forums.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: WMed is committed to ensuring that all students have equitable access to the medical education experience. We aim to support students in addressing barriers they may encounter due to a disability. For more information, please visit: https://wmed.edu/accommodations
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The WMed Wellness Initiative, launched in 2019, expands our school’s promotion of well-being and excellence at both an individual and organizational level with the aim to support, educate, and inspire all members of the medical school community to nurture mind-body-spirit wellness for themselves, others, and the community as a whole. This focus goes hand-in-hand with WMed’s vision of health equity for all in Southwest Michigan through innovation in the practice and study of medicine. By bringing wellness to the forefront, we help create a healthy climate which supports all members of the WMed community to embody our values.

Learn more at: https://wmed.edu/wellness and wmed.edu/studentwellness
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
We seek to create an inspiring environment to learn, teach, and work that embodies our values and to promote a climate of cultural and psychological safety, equity, cultural humility, engagement, trust, accountability, recognition, wellness, belonging, and cohesion.

Learn more: https://wmed.edu/ourculture
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: A vehicle is not required, but is strongly recommended.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Dress for the classroom is casual. Dress for clinical experiences is professional.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Faculty have an open-door policy, and students are encouraged to contact faculty directly in person, by email, or phone. Free tutoring is available.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Clinical experiences begin early, including Medical First Responder training beginning in the first month and through Introductory Clinical Experiences throughout the Foundations curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Most instruction is delivered in team-based learning and small group activities. Simulation training is introduced from the first days at WMed and is emphasized throughout the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical experiences begin as an M1. Students complete core clinical rotations during M3 at our affiliate hospitals and clinics. Clinical Application Curriculum: https://wmed.edu/mdprogramclinicalapps
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Lecture attendance is optional, and lectures are also live streamed and recorded. Attendance is required at team-based curricular events and clinical components.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
WMed recognizes the need for innovative medical education to meet the changing health care needs of individuals, our communities, and the global society. Our team-based curriculum promotes a learner-centered approach that comes to life through adult learning principles of self-directed, peer-supported, and experiential inquiry and learning.

The curriculum is divided into two phases: 
Foundations of Medicine ( https://wmed.edu/mdprogramfoundations )
Clinical Applications ( https://wmed.edu/mdprogramclinicalapps )
Clinical encounters are part of the continuum of learning that builds throughout the four years of medical school experience.

During Foundations of Medicine, the focus is on the basic sciences integrated with introductory clinical medicine. This integration comes through the longitudinal Clinical Experiences course, clinical skills training that is part of the Profession of Medicine course, and the clinical correlation components within each organ-system course. Learn more: https://wmed.edu/MD-curriculum
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Our students are trained to succeed in any medical specialty of their choosing. Clinical training includes extensive primary care experiences in modern facilities with contemporary practice models. The WMed Clinics are accredited by the Joint Commission, which has additionally certified the WMed Clinics as a Primary Care Medical Home. This designation recognizes our ability to deliver coordinated and comprehensive primary care to participants of all ages & children, youth, and adults. This model is a partnership between individuals and families within a healthcare setting, which allows for a more efficient use of resources and improves the quality of patient outcomes. Rural health rotations are provided as part of the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Numerous opportunities exist for students to participate in clinical research, community-based research, basic science research, outcomes-based research, and educational research. Small class sizes lead to opportunities to connect and explore research options throughout the medical school and Kalamazoo community. 

Learn more about research at WMed: wmed.edu/research
A list of WMed student scholarly publications is available at: https://wmed.edu/studentresearchactivities
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Opportunities are built into the curriculum and through student organizations and interest groups.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Many WMed students choose to pursue research areas of interest. Learn more: https://wmed.edu/studentresearchactivities
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: WMed has a major affiliation with Beacon Health System and Bronson Healthcare. Learn more at: https://wmed.edu/mdprogramclinicalapps#clinicalaffiliates
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Grading during Foundation coursework (M1 and M2) is pass/fail. Grading during Clinical Applications (M3 and M4) is honors/high pass/pass/fail.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Western Michigan University Homer Stryker M.D. School of Medicine (WMed) is a private medical school created through the collaboration of Western Michigan University and Kalamazoo's two teaching hospitals, Beacon Health System and Bronson Healthcare. WMed is a testament to the vision and dedication of our community, and we are built on a legacy of innovation and excellence in health sciences and the strengths of extraordinary collaborators. Our goal for our graduates is to realize their individual potential to be great clinicians, leaders, educators, advocates, and researchers. 

Learn more: https://wmed.edu/fromthedean
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Mission: 
WMed is committed to excellence and health equity through transformative medical education, high-quality patient care, innovative research, and community partnerships within a just culture of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.

Vision: 
Health equity for all in Southwest Michigan through innovation in the practice and study of medicine.

Values: 
Together We: 
Excel with integrity and professionalism
Champion safety and belonging
Listen, collaborate, and serve with respect and compassion

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: More information is available at https://wmed.edu/app under Letters of Reference.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Two of the letters are preferred to be from faculty members who have been the applicant's undergraduate or graduate instructors or mentors, or employment supervisors in the case of non-traditional applicants. If students apply from a university that provides a composite letter from a premedical advisory program, the composite letter will be accepted in lieu of the two letters recommended from faculty.

Most importantly, we encourage letters from those who know you well and can provide insights about your skills, attributes and values along with your personal qualities like work ethic, attitude, and motivation for a medical career.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Interviews will be held virtually beginning late September 2026 for the Class of 2031.

The goal of our Interview Day is not only for us to get to know you, but for you to get to know us and start picturing yourself as a WMed student. Applicants invited to interview will be given access to videos, links, and information to review before attending the session so the virtual time together can be used to answer specific questions and focus on your specific areas of interest. The virtual Interview Day will include plenty of time with current students and faculty.

Learn more: https://wmed.edu/app
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Interview invitations begin in August. Interviews are held from late September through mid March.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Interviews for the Class of 2031 beginning in June 2027 will be held virtually. Interview sessions will include a traditional one-on-one open file interview in addition to a group activity. More details will be provided in the interview invitation.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Interviews for the class beginning in June 2027 will be held virtually.

medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: To be invited to complete the secondary application process, we require a minimum MCAT score of 499 and a minimum GPA of 3.0.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: To be invited to complete the secondary application process, we require a minimum GPA of 3.0 and minimum MCAT score of 499.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: We look for applicants with upward trending GPAs. For those who have 24 or more hours of post-bacc or graduate-level science coursework, we will replace the undergraduate science GPA with this higher-level work.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: WMed will accept all community college coursework. WMed does not have required coursework, rather coursework we recommend applicants have completed before matriculation.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants may upload update letters along with letters of intent/interest to their WMU Admissions portal. We ask that update letters are only uploaded when there has been significant changes to an applicant's experiences/research since submitting their primary application. We ask that letters of interest/intent are reserved for if WMed is truly one of the top 2-3 schools an applicant would attend if accepted.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Prior to matriculation, a candidate must attest that they have read the school’s technical standards and to the best of their knowledge can meet them with or without reasonable accommodation. WMed provides reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities via the Office of Student Affairs and the Accommodations Committee.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
WMed provides individualized financial planning assistance for each student. Financial aid includes availability of institutional scholarships that are awarded based on need and/or merit. All students who are accepted are automatically considered for merit scholarships and will be notified of the steps to apply for need-based financial aid.

Additional Financial Aid information available at: https://wmed.edu/financial-aid
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy:
Tuition is charged annually for each of the four academic years and is assessed in two equal installments, with one-half of the annual tuition due at the beginning of each term. Tuition includes the cost of disability insurance, professional liability (malpractice) insurance, software licenses for some required software and web-based resources, fees for some examinations, consumable training supplies, and other miscellaneous expenses.

For first-year students, the first tuition payment is due by the first Wednesday in August, and the second tuition payment is due by the second Wednesday in January. For second-year, third-year, and fourth-year students, tuition payments are due by the second Wednesday of each term.

A complete financial calendar is provided for each class of students, including the class of 2020, in the Medical Student Handbook.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Candidates can be considered for the Master's in Biomedical Sciences by completing a direct application to the program or by invitation based on AMCAS and secondary application materials. The one-year MBS program is designed to strengthen understanding in basic science material, providing a stronger foundation as the student enters medical school. The MBS program includes a linkage into the medical program, as matriculating students are conditionally accepted to the MD program for the following year.

The MBS program offers a full-tuition scholarship to each matriculating student, and many students receive a cost of living stipend as well, to ensure there are no financial obstacles in preparing for the MD program.

Learn more at: https://wmed.edu/education 

Contact the Office of Admissions at admissions@wmed.edu.

medSchoolAssessments.assessmentAdditionalInformation: Designed to learn more about your attributes, the multiple choice assessment includes 45 questions with 20 minutes to complete the assessment. Free to applicants with link provided during Secondary Application process. Required in order to complete the Secondary Application.

Unique to WMed, the Phone Interview is focused on your personal attributes and lasts about 30 minutes. Approximately 900 candidates are invited, and interviewers are blind to all application materials.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: The waitlist is live, unranked, and reviewed at each Admissions Committee meeting throughout the cycle. Candidates on the waitlist may be offered admission at any point in the cycle.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
There are no required prerequisite courses for admission to WMed.

WMed seeks applicants who have a broad-based and quality pre-medical experience that includes courses in the natural and biological sciences, social sciences, and humanities. The course of study should include significant experience in upper-level science coursework. Majoring in the sciences is not required. Undergraduate coursework must be completed at an institution accredited by a regional institutional accreditor in the US. 

Applicants are encouraged to gain a strong hard science foundation that will benefit them during medical school and throughout their careers. The recommended courses have been selected to prepare you to succeed in our curriculum.

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
WMed uses holistic, mission-aligned review at each stage of the admission process. Applicants meeting the minimum academic criteria are invited to complete the secondary application, which includes supplemental essays and an online assessment focused on the candidate's personal attributes and fit with WMed. Selected candidates are invited to participate in a phone interview designed to further assess the applicant's attributes. The final step is the Interview Day, where applicants participate in both a traditional one-on-one interview and a group interview activity.

WMed seeks leaders with the personal attributes and characteristics to excel as physicians, and who are team players, can problem solve, demonstrate compassion and empathy, are committed to serving others, have strong oral and written communication skills, and make decisions with integrity. WMed's curriculum is focused on team-based learning, and we look for these qualities to build strong teams at WMed and beyond.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: We encourage depth and breadth of clinical exposure. This exposure can be gained through shadowing, volunteering, or working in the healthcare field.
